### **Short Story (narrative form)**  

There was once a man who lived in a marble house by a silent pond.  
He wasn’t born cruel, only convinced that the world should see him shining.  

Each morning he polished his reflection until it bowed to his expectations. He spoke gently to his own image — as if it were the only friend who never contradicted him.  

But one day, a whisper began in the wind. It spoke of a shadow that followed him wherever he went. He said nothing. He believed if he stayed very still, perhaps the world would forget the echo of his past footsteps.  

He sought counsel not in truth but in comfort. “It was only a misunderstanding,” he told his reflection. “They’ve exaggerated it.” The mirror nodded back, obedient as always.  

Then came the visitor — a frog by the pond, wide-eyed and ugly, croaking a single word: *“Choice.”*  
The man laughed. “I don’t make choices,” he said. “I am the choice others make.”  

So he kissed the frog, not to save it, but to prove he could still transform something.  
But this time, the spell worked the other way around.  

His lips met the frog’s skin and the world rippled. When the pond settled, it was the frog who stood in fine clothes, blinking in the light — and the man who sank beneath the surface, his reflection breaking into a thousand bubbles.  

Now, deep below, in the stillness of the pond, a frog watches a man’s face in the water.  
Every morning, it asks the same question the wind once asked him:  
“Was the crown worth the silence?”  

And the reflection, still handsome but fading, never answers.
